statements.text: [[revenue|Revenue]] grew 4.9% in the year ended February 1, 2026, to $11.1 billion. This means the company sold more than the year before.
In the [[quarter|quarter]] ended August 2, 2026, revenue was $2.4 billion, down 4.3% from the same quarter a year earlier.
[[net-income|Net income]], the profit left after all costs and taxes, fell 13% to $1.6 billion in the year ended February 1, 2026.
After paying for the products it sold, the company kept about $57 of every $100 of sales. This is called its [[gross-margin|gross margin]].
Out of every $100 of sales, about $14 was left as profit after all costs and taxes. This is called its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].
Its day-to-day business brought in $1.6 billion of cash in the year ended February 1, 2026. This is called [[cash-from-operations|cash from operations]].
On August 2, 2026, the company had $1.4 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash and cash equivalents]], money it can use quickly.

figures.label: cash, including cash set aside for specific uses

statements.text: On August 2, 2026, the company had $3.9 billion in cash and other assets it expects to use within a year, against $1.8 billion of bills due within a year. That is about $2.19 for every $1 it owes soon, more than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
It owned $8.5 billion in [[assets|assets]] and owed $3.7 billion in [[total-liabilities|total liabilities]], so it owned about $2.30 for every $1 it owed.

Its business brought in $1.6 billion of cash in the year ended February 1, 2026 and spent $680.8 million on [[capital-expenditure|buildings and equipment]], leaving $921.7 million of [[free-cash-flow|free cash flow]]: money it could use for dividends, buybacks, paying down debt or growing.
Free cash flow was smaller than its [[net-income|net income]] ($1.6 billion) that year, meaning less of its accounting profit turned into spare cash.
In the year ended February 1, 2026, the company spent $1.2 billion buying back its own shares ([[share-buyback|buybacks]]) and invested $680.8 million in buildings and equipment.
It earned about $34 of profit for every $100 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] in the year ended February 1, 2026. This is its [[return-on-equity|return on equity]] (34%).
[[eps|Earnings per share]] (diluted) fell 9.4% to $13.26 in the year ended February 1, 2026.
Over the 5 years to February 1, 2026, its [[operating-margin|operating margin]] fell to 19.9%, from 21.3%.
In the year to February 2026, it made $11.1 billion in [[revenue|sales]], 4.9% more than the year before. Sales in its latest three months (to August 2026) were down 4.3% on a year earlier.
In the year to February 2026, it kept $1.6 billion as [[net-income|profit]] after paying all its costs and taxes: about $14 of every $100 it made in sales, its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].

On August 2, 2026, for every $1 of bills due within a year, it had about $2.19 in cash and other things it expected to turn into cash in that time: more than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
On August 2, 2026, it held $1.4 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash]].

statements.text: In the year to February 2026, its everyday business brought in $1.6 billion in [[cash-from-operations|cash]]. After paying for [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]], $921.7 million was [[free-cash-flow|left over]].
In the year to February 2026, its biggest uses of money were: [[share-buyback|buying back its own shares]]: $1.2 billion; and [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]]: $680.8 million.
